# What a site installer package is

This page is for anyone who chooses a site package in the setup wizard, sets one in `kickstart.ini`, or passes one to
`exp:install --package`, and wants to know what that choice really is. It answers: what is a site package, what does
it contain, what does it leave to other packages, and which ones exist.

## Contents

1. [In one paragraph](#in-one-paragraph)
2. [The three parts of a site package](#the-three-parts-of-a-site-package)
3. [A worked example: sevenx_multisite](#a-worked-example-sevenx_multisite)
4. [The packages a site package requires](#the-packages-a-site-package-requires)
5. [The site packages of 6.0.15](#the-site-packages-of-6015)

## In one paragraph

A **site installer package**, or **site package**, is an Exponential package whose `package.xml` says
`<type value="site"/>`. It describes a whole starting site, but it carries very little of that site itself: it
names the packages that hold the content classes, the content, the extensions and the designs
(`<dependencies><requires>`), and it carries PHP install scripts (`<settings><settings-file>`) that the installer
calls to write the siteaccess settings, roles and preferences. The setup wizard, the kickstarter and `exp:install`
only offer packages of this type as the site to install
(`eZStepSiteTypes::fetchAvailableSitePackages()` filters on `'type' => 'site'`, and the remote list keeps only index
entries with `type="site"`).

## The three parts of a site package

| Part | In `package.xml` | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Description | `<name>`, `<summary>`, `<description>`, `<vendor>`, `<version>`, `<licence>`, thumbnail in `<files>` | What the wizard shows on the site selection page |
| Requirements | `<dependencies><requires><require type="ezpackage" .../>` | The packages that are fetched with it and installed |
| Install scripts | `<settings><settings-file filename="..."/>`, files in `settings/` | PHP functions the Create sites step calls at fixed points |

Every site package of the 6.0.15 index has `install_type="import"` and an empty `<install/>`: the site package itself
installs nothing. What ends up on the site comes from the packages it requires and from its install scripts. See
[Import versus install](import-versus-install.md).

## A worked example: sevenx_multisite

`sevenx_multisite` is the default site package of `exp:install` and of `exp:kickstarter ini --yes`. Its source is the
folder `packages/sevenx_multisite/` of [se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage).
Its archive on the package server contains:

```text
documents/LICENCE
files/default/image/logo.png
files/default/thumbnail/thumbnail.png
package.xml
settings/ini-admin.php
settings/ini-common.php
settings/ini-site.php
settings/install-scripts.php
settings/post-install-fix.php
settings/preferences.php
settings/roles.php
settings/sevenx-multi-site-installer.php
```

The parts of its `package.xml` that matter here (shortened; the maintainer e-mail is left out):

```xml
<package version="6.0.15-0" development="false" is_active="true" install_type="import">
  <name>sevenx_multisite</name>
  <vendor>7x</vendor>
  <type value="site" />
  <version>
    <number>6.0</number>
    <release>15-stable</release>
  </version>
  <licence>GPL</licence>
  <dependencies>
    <requires>
      <require type="ezpackage" name="sevenx_classes" min-version="5.1" />
      <require type="ezpackage" name="sevenx_multisite_democontent" min-version="5.1" />
    </requires>
  </dependencies>
  <settings>
    <settings-file filename='ini-site.php'/>
    <settings-file filename='ini-admin.php'/>
    <settings-file filename='ini-common.php'/>
    <settings-file filename='sevenx-multi-site-installer.php'/>
    <settings-file filename='install-scripts.php'/>
    <settings-file filename='roles.php'/>
    <settings-file filename='preferences.php'/>
  </settings>
  <install />
  <uninstall />
</package>
```

So installing "sevenx_multisite" means: import it, import and install `sevenx_classes` (the content classes) and
`sevenx_multisite_democontent` (content classes and the demo content), and run the installer class in
`sevenx-multi-site-installer.php` through the hooks in `install-scripts.php`, `ini-*.php`, `roles.php` and
`preferences.php`. The details of that installer are in
[The multisite installer script](../sevenx-multisite/the-multisite-installer-script.md).

> **Note**
> The layout rows (`explayouts_*` tables) of a sevenx_multisite site are not in any package. The installer seeds
> them from the `share/` folders of extensions; see
> [Layouts data and share DBA files](../sevenx-multisite/layouts-data-and-share-dba.md).

## The packages a site package requires

The required packages are ordinary packages with `install_type="install"` (or none, which means the same) and real
install items. In the 6.0.15 index they are:

| Type | Packages | Install items they carry |
|---|---|---|
| `contentclass` | `sevenx_classes`, `ezwebin_classes`, `ezflow_classes`, `ezdemo_classes` | `ezcontentclass`, one per class |
| `contentobject` | `sevenx_multisite_democontent(_clean)`, `cjw_multisite_democontent`, `sevenx_democontent(_clean)`, `sevenx_banners`, the `ezwebin_`, `ezflow_` and `ezdemo_` content packages | `ezcontentobject` (one item for all objects), some also `ezcontentclass` |
| `extension` | `sevenx_extension`, `ezwebin_extension`, `ezflow_extension`, `ezdemo_extension`, `ezpaypal_extension`, `ezwt_extension`, `ezstarrating_extension`, `ezgmaplocation_extension` | `ezextension` |
| `sitestyle` | `sevenx_design_blue`, `_cleangray`, `_gray`, the `ezwebin_design_` three, `ezflow_design` | `ezfile` (with `install_type="import"`) |

Each type and handler is explained in [Package types](package-types.md) and
[Install items and handlers](install-items-and-handlers.md).

## The site packages of 6.0.15

The index at `https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml` lists twelve
packages with `type="site"`:

| Package | Summary in the index | Requires (count) |
|---|---|---|
| `sevenx_multisite` | 7x MultiSite Default Installation | 2 |
| `sevenx_multisite_clean` | 7x MultiSite Default Installation (without demo content) | 2 |
| `cjw_multisite` | CJW Multisite | 2 |
| `sevenx_site` | 7x Simple Website Interface | 11 |
| `sevenx_site_clean` | 7x Simple Website Interface (without demo content) | 10 |
| `ezflow_site`, `ezflow_site_clean` | eZ Flow, eZ Flow (without demo content) | 9 each |
| `ezwebin_site` | Website Interface | 11 |
| `ezwebin_site_clean` | Website Interface (without demo content) | 10 |
| `ezdemo_site`, `ezdemo_site_clean` | Exponential Demo Site, ... (without demo content) | 8 each |
| `plain_site` | Plain site | 0 |

A `_clean` variant requires the `_clean` content package instead of the demo content one. The per-package pages are
[sevenx_multisite](../sevenx-multisite/README.md) and [cjw_multisite](../cjw-multisite/README.md); the full list of
files on the server is in [What is on the package server](../package-server/what-is-on-the-package-server.md).

## What a site package is not

- **Not an extension.** Extensions are installed from Composer or Git, or from packages of type `extension`; a site
  package only names them.
- **Not the whole site.** Classes and content come from the packages it requires; layouts of sevenx_multisite come
  from extension share files.
- **Not a backup.** A site package builds a new site. To move an existing site, see
  [ezpm, the package manager on the command line](../../../features/6.0/ezpm-package-manager-cli.md).
- **Not installed by itself in Setup > Packages.** Its package page says there is nothing to install, because its
  install type is `import`.
